title: Stored Procedure Parameters
description: Learn how to create stored procedures with input parameters, optional parameters, and default values.

data.text: Stored procedure parameters allow you to pass values into a procedure. The result changes based on the parameter values. Every parameter must start with the @ sign.

data.title: Stored procedure with one parameter
data.content: Finds products with list price >= a minimum value.
data.code:
ALTER PROCEDURE uspFindProducts(@min_list_price AS DECIMAL)
AS
BEGIN
    SELECT
        product_name,
        list_price
    FROM
        production.products
    WHERE
        list_price >= @min_list_price
    ORDER BY
        list_price;
END;

data.title: Execute with one parameter
data.content: Passes 100 as the minimum list price.

data.title: Stored procedure with two parameters
data.content: Finds products within a price range.
data.code:
ALTER PROCEDURE uspFindProducts(
    @min_list_price AS DECIMAL,
    @max_list_price AS DECIMAL
)
AS
BEGIN
    SELECT
        product_name,
        list_price
    FROM
        production.products
    WHERE
        list_price >= @min_list_price AND
        list_price <= @max_list_price
    ORDER BY
        list_price;
END;

data.title: Execute with multiple parameters
data.content: Passes both min and max price values.

data.text: When a procedure has multiple parameters, use named parameters for clarity:

data.title: Named parameters
data.content: Executes with named parameters for clarity.

data.title: Optional parameters with defaults
data.content: Creates optional parameters with default values.

data.title: Execute with optional parameter skipped
data.content: Calls procedure without specifying optional parameters.

data.title: Stored Procedure Parameters Key Points
points: Parameters start with @ and have a specified data type.
Use named parameters for clarity with multiple parameters.
NULL can be used as a default value for flexible filtering.
